+With Compare Models enabled and the experimental `sessions.chat.compareAgents.tools.enabled` setting opted into (default: `false`), Agents-window agents can use `getComparisonModels` to discover provider-local fixed model selections and configuration schemas, then `createModelComparison` to launch one scenario with two to ten attempts and an optional Judge and Synthesizer. Creation uses the caller's host, canonical project workspace, and provider-owned permission intent, including when the caller is a nested chat. Explicit folderless comparisons omit the workspace, branch, Judge, and Synthesizer. Creation uses normal tool approval, revalidates the prepared configuration before launch, and leaves the evaluator chat focused. Comparison participants cannot recursively launch comparisons. The comparison service remains the single owner of participant creation and lifecycle; these client tools do not invoke or change the native Agent Host `create_session` tool's private orchestration counters.

`listModelComparisons` reads persisted comparison records independently of sidebar filters, with bounded pages and optional archive, workspace, and ID filters. `readModelComparison` is read-only and available to any eligible agent in the window, not just the comparison's creator or Judge. It exposes the original task, stable attempt numbers including failed launches, per-chat state and bounded change evidence, available completion metrics, and the persisted structured verdict. Participant records include exact context targets for reachable attempt, Judge, and synthesis chats. `get_session_context` owns follow-up trajectory retrieval with its existing summary, digest, full, and recent-turn limits; unsupported providers and other hosts have explicit unavailable reasons rather than guessed targets. Archived records remain readable even when live worktrees or transcripts no longer exist.

-These evaluator tools do not change the Judge/Synthesizer authorization of `readAttemptComparison` or the Judge-only write authority of `completeAttemptComparison`. Disabling comparison setup removes evaluator tools and prevents new launches, while existing participant tools retain their completion/restoration behavior. Evaluation collections use existing parent-session organization; agents orchestrate multiple tool calls and produce reports without a separate collection store, scheduler, or reporting UI.

+These evaluator tools do not change the Judge/Synthesizer authorization of `readAttemptComparison` or the Judge-only write authority of `completeAttemptComparison`. Disabling the evaluator-tool setting removes all four evaluator tools and rejects pending invocations, including launches awaiting approval, without disabling manual comparisons or existing participant tools. Disabling comparison setup also removes evaluator tools and prevents new launches, while existing participant tools retain their completion/restoration behavior. Evaluation collections use existing parent-session organization; agents orchestrate multiple tool calls and produce reports without a separate collection store, scheduler, or reporting UI.

Attempts inherit the current workspace, branch, agent, and permissions. Done and Next stay disabled until two to ten models are checked, and the footer shows how many are selected. Use Tab to reach Done and Next. In Judge, optionally select a model to review the attempts and recommend a winner. Leave Judge unselected and activate Done to run attempts without review. With a Judge selected, activate Next to choose an optional Synthesizer. Without a Synthesizer, review is available but synthesis is not. Activate a selected model again to clear it. Back preserves your choices. Done returns to the composer; activate Run N Attempts to launch. Escape closes the picker without launching. Open the comparison parent in the Sessions list to open every available attempt in a resizable grid. With two attempt panes, both chat inputs remain visible. With three or more, only the active attempt pane shows its chat input; focus another attempt pane to show its input. Screen-reader optimized mode keeps every attempt input visible. After the Judge finishes, its chat shows a scorecard: the winning model with the Judge's explanation, then a row for each attempt, recommended first, with a summary of its validation checks such as Tests passed or Not run, total time, and tokens. Use Tab to reach the Checks column header to hear what the checks cover. Focus the comparison result and use Open Accessible View{0} to read its verdict and attempt metrics as plain text. Use Tab to reach the attempt rows and Up Arrow or Down Arrow to move between them, then press Enter or Space to expand a row with the Judge's reasoning, what is worth keeping, gaps, each check's result, and Open Attempt N. Each row also has an Open button after its metrics that opens that attempt's session. Activate Open Attempt to open the recommended attempt, or use its adjacent dropdown to open another attempt. When synthesis is available, Synthesize starts the Judge's default plan. Open its More Actions menu and choose Additional Synthesis Instructions to enter requirements that are remembered and applied to recommended synthesis. Activate Start Synthesis with Instructions, or press Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on macOS) in that field, to start the recommended plan with those requirements. The additional instructions guide a new synthesis session and do not modify the original attempts.", '<keybinding:editor.action.accessibleView>'));
